title: Understanding Proper Horizontal Drainage Slope
description: Achieving the correct slope on horizontal drain lines is critical for maintaining efficient waste transport in DWV systems. Standard plumbing codes generally require a minimum uniform fall—typically one-quarter inch per foot for smaller diameter pipes—to maintain liquid velocity. If a drain pipe lacks adequate pitch, waste water flows too slowly, allowing heavy solids and grease to settle on the pipe invert. Conversely, excessive slope causes liquids to rush ahead, leaving solid waste behind to accumulate. Maintaining consistent alignment, using proper pipe hangers, and verifying grade with a digital level ensures long-term self-scouring performance.
